Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame lock deliver a noticeably smoother feel than 30 fps while keeping power draw moderate; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps image quality acceptable. High textures and ambient occlusion on give a good visual result without overtaxing the GPU.

profiles.Summary: NieR:Automata runs well on the Steam Deck with a platinum ProtonDB rating, and the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the game's minimum GTX 770 requirement, making a stable 60 fps achievable at medium settings. The game is Steam Deck Playable with partial controller support, and most players report a smooth experience out of the box with Default Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements against the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class). On first run, check frame rate in the open desert area and during large enemy encounters — these are typically the most demanding scenes — and drop to Optimal if the 60 fps cap is not holding.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps GPU load minimal; the 7 W TDP and 30 Hz lock push battery life as far as possible. NieR:Automata is still enjoyable at 30 fps, though fast combat may feel less responsive — step up to Optimal if it feels sluggish.

KnownIssues: The game's built-in graphics options are limited, with no native shadow quality slider or granular AA controls in some versions.
Partial controller support means some menus or UI prompts may display keyboard/mouse hints rather than controller glyphs.
Occasional stuttering reported during open-area transitions, typical of this engine on PC hardware.
The popular FAR (Fix Automata Resolution) PC mod is not recommended for use under Proton on Steam Deck.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with high settings is within reach of the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU for most scenes, though busy open areas or dense particle effects may dip into the low 50s. Anti-aliasing is left off as the game's built-in TAA can cause blurring; the native resolution keeps the image sharp without it.

Optimal.Notes: This profile hits a near-locked 60 fps across most of the game with good image quality; FSR upscaling from 1152x720 recovers GPU headroom while keeping the picture sharp on the OLED screen. Shader stutters on first run should resolve after a short play session.

profiles.Summary: NieR:Automata runs well on the Steam Deck at Platinum ProtonDB tier, delivering a smooth experience at 60 fps with medium settings out of the box. The game's PC minimum GPU requirements are within the Deck's capability, though the engine has some known quirks on Linux/Proton that may require a community patch or workaround for best results.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2017 PC requirements (minimum GPU ~GTX 770, recommended ~GTX 980), its Platinum ProtonDB tier, and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU performance class. On your first run, check the frame counter in a busy open-world area (the City Ruins or the desert) and drop to the Optimal or MaxBattery profile if you see sustained dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at a sub-native resolution with FSR upscaling and a 6 W TDP cap keeps the Deck very cool and quiet; 30 fps is stable throughout. Half-rate shading is skipped as the game's fast combat makes shading artifacts distracting.

KnownIssues: The game ships without an official borderless/fullscreen fix; the FAR (Fix Automata Resolution) mod is widely recommended on PC but may complicate Proton setup — use with caution on Deck.
Some players report stuttering during large open-area transitions due to shader compilation on first run; this typically clears up after the first play session.
The game's built-in resolution options are limited; non-standard resolutions like 1280x800 may not appear natively in the in-game menu.
Partial controller support means some menus may require touchscreen or mouse input; the Steam Deck's touchpad can be used as a workaround.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high settings is achievable given the game's 2017 vintage engine; the Deck's GPU comfortably exceeds the minimum spec, but uncapped frametimes can vary in busy areas so expect occasional dips to the mid-50s. Battery life is short at full TDP — best used plugged in or for short sessions.
